note: Tools communities use alongside their main platform, grouped by kind. A tool can belong to several categories.

categories.label: Deliberation & decision-making
categories.description: Tools that structure group discussion, proposal-making, and collective decisions.

categories.label: Voting & polling
categories.description: Tools for gathering member preferences through votes, polls, or ranked choices.

categories.label: Surveys & feedback
categories.description: Tools for collecting structured input, feedback, or research from members.

categories.label: Trust & safety
categories.description: Tools that help communities detect, investigate, review, and act on harmful content or behavior.

categories.label: Moderation bots & filters
categories.description: Automated tools that enforce community rules, filter content, or assist human moderators.

categories.label: Announcements & newsletters
categories.description: Tools for broadcasting updates, newsletters, or one-way communications to members.

categories.label: Documentation & wikis
categories.description: Tools for collaboratively writing, organizing, and sharing community knowledge and processes.

categories.label: Events & calendars
categories.description: Tools for scheduling, organizing, and managing community events and shared calendars.

categories.label: Funding & finance
categories.description: Tools for collecting dues, managing community finances, or running fundraising campaigns.

categories.label: Identity & access
categories.description: Tools for verifying identity, managing membership credentials, or gating access to community spaces.

items.label: Airtable
items.description: Spreadsheet-database hybrid often used to track member applications, feedback, and community data.

items.label: All Our Ideas
items.description: Pairwise voting tool that surfaces collective priorities from open-ended member input.

items.label: BookStack
items.description: Self-hosted, open-source wiki and documentation platform organized as books, chapters, and pages.

items.label: Buttondown
items.description: Simple, privacy-focused newsletter tool popular with independent writers and community organizers.

items.label: Cal.com
items.description: Open-source scheduling tool for booking meetings and coordinating availability across a community.

items.label: Cobudget
items.description: Collaborative budgeting tool that lets community members propose and fund initiatives together.

items.label: Collab.Land
items.description: Token-gated access management for Discord and Telegram communities in Web3 ecosystems.

items.label: Confluence
items.description: Team wiki and documentation platform from Atlassian, widely used in organizations.

items.label: Consider.it
items.description: Visual deliberation tool that shows where people stand on proposals and what arguments they find compelling.

items.label: Consul
items.description: Open-source participatory democracy platform for proposals, debates, and voting, used by municipalities.

items.label: Coop (ROOST)
items.description: Open-source human review console for content moderation with queue orchestration and CSAM/NCMEC reporting workflows.

items.label: CryptPad
items.description: Open-source, end-to-end encrypted collaborative document and wiki suite with no account required.

items.label: Decidim
items.description: Participatory democracy platform with proposals, debates, participatory budgeting, and assemblies.

items.label: Donorbox
items.description: Donation and fundraising tool for nonprofits and community organizations with recurring giving support.

items.label: Eventbrite
items.description: Event ticketing and registration platform for both free and paid community events.

items.label: Ghost
items.description: Open-source publishing platform with newsletter, membership, and paid subscription features.

items.label: GitBook
items.description: Documentation platform for publishing structured knowledge bases, guides, and internal wikis.

items.label: Google Forms
items.description: Simple survey and polling tool, requires a Google account.

items.label: Guild
items.description: Access gating for community spaces based on token ownership, role, or credential, popular in Web3.

items.label: Hasher-Matcher-Actioner (HMA)
items.description: Open-source hash matching system from Meta for detecting known harmful content such as CSAM and TVEC.

items.label: HedgeDoc
items.description: Self-hosted, open-source collaborative markdown editor for real-time document co-authoring.

items.label: Hive Moderation
items.description: AI-driven image, text, and video moderation API for platform safety teams.

items.label: Kialo
items.description: Structured pro/con debate mapping tool that helps groups reason through complex decisions together.

items.label: Listmonk
items.description: Self-hosted, open-source newsletter and mailing list manager with no per-subscriber fees.

items.label: Llama Guard
items.description: Open-source safety classifier from Meta for detecting unsafe content in LLM inputs and outputs, adaptable to custom policies.

items.label: Loomio
items.description: Structured discussion threads with voting (consent, polls, proposals), popular with co-ops and nonprofits.

items.label: Luma
items.description: Event management and community calendar tool with RSVP, ticketing, and email reminders.

items.label: Mailchimp
items.description: Email marketing and newsletter platform with list management, automation, and campaign analytics.

items.label: MediaWiki
items.description: Open-source wiki software that powers Wikipedia, suitable for large community knowledge bases.

items.label: Mentimeter
items.description: Live polling and Q&A tool for community calls and town halls.

items.label: Mobilizon
items.description: Open-source, federated event organizing platform designed as a privacy-respecting alternative to Facebook Events.

items.label: Notion
items.description: All-in-one workspace for notes, wikis, databases, and project management.

items.label: Open Collective
items.description: Transparent fundraising and financial management platform for communities, collectives, and open-source projects.

items.label: OpenAI Moderation API
items.description: Free API from OpenAI that classifies text across harmful content categories including hate speech, self-harm, and violence.

items.label: Osprey (ROOST)
items.description: Open-source rules engine for real-time event processing and behavioral investigation, donated by Discord.

items.label: Ozone
items.description: Open-source moderation tool from Bluesky Social for running independent labeling services on the AT Protocol.

items.label: Patreon
items.description: Membership and subscription platform for communities to offer tiered supporter access and benefits.

items.label: Perspective API
items.description: Machine learning API from Google/Jigsaw that scores text for toxicity and other harmful attributes.

items.label: Polis
items.description: AI-assisted opinion mapping that surfaces areas of cross-group agreement, often used in civic contexts.

items.label: pretix
items.description: Open-source ticketing and registration platform with access control and membership check-in features.

items.label: Remesh
items.description: AI-assisted large-group deliberation platform that surfaces themes and consensus in real time.

items.label: Slido
items.description: Live Q&A and polling tool for meetings and events, with audience interaction features.

items.label: Snapshot
items.description: Off-chain, token-weighted governance voting used by DAOs and Web3 communities.

items.label: Substack
items.description: Newsletter and publication platform with paid subscription support and community comment sections.

items.label: Tally
items.description: Free form builder with a clean interface, no account required for respondents.

items.label: Typeform
items.description: Form and survey builder for async preference gathering and community input.
